notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus one extra general search (seven in total); none was refused. None returned a statement by Golden on AI risk, superintelligence, a pause, China talks or AI safety. The site-restricted search returned no golden.house.gov pages about AI. Not a statement, so left out: a Newsweek article ('Beijing looms large over American AI politics', apparently September 2026, https://www.newsweek.com/ai-politics/beijing-china-us-government-ai-politics-artificial-intelligence-12501825, opened) says that in Newsweek's AI Policy Scorecard Golden is 'the lead Democrat' in the 'Boosters' group and ranks second behind Senator John Fetterman among top-ranked AI boosters in his party; it gives no words of his own, and the scorecard method is not explained. The same article and other results say he is retiring at the end of this term (he did not run in 2026). An AFL-CIO scorecard search result lists a 12 June 2025 vote on an amendment to bar state and local AI laws (H.R. 4, Rescissions Act of 2025), but the snippet did not show how he voted and the page was not opened, so it is not recorded. The Bangor Daily News roundup of Maine politicians responding to AI warnings (16 September 2026) was opened and does not mention him. Carried over from the earlier attempt: his official press release listing (pages 1 to 10, 21 May 2025 to 12 November 2026) was checked directly and showed no release mentioning AI, data centers or China in titles or excerpts; the listing jumped from 14 July 2026 to 9 June 2026 between pages 2 and 3, so releases in that window may have been missed; January to May 2025 releases, hearing remarks (Armed Services Committee) and floor speeches were not checked. The FastDemocracy cosponsor list for the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (12 cosponsors, all Democrats) does not include him; that page was read in the earlier attempt, not re-opened this time.
